purpose: Reproduce and isolate the N=7/N=8 Nav2 liveness failure reported in PR #25 before changing any protocol behaviour.

mechanism.summary: isLive() compares a peer's last observed heartbeat tick against the receiver's OWN logical tick, with a 6-tick window. A healthy peer's heartbeat is only delivered through the Fast DDS bridge, so when the transport backs up the peer looks dead even though it is running.
mechanism.selfDeliveryIsSynchronous: OwnershipPeer.send() also calls receive() locally, so a peer always sees its own heartbeat at age 0. Only remote heartbeats traverse the bridge. The measurement shows self at age 0 and every remote peer at age 8-211, which isolates the fault to remote delivery rather than the protocol clock.
mechanism.notPhysicalExecution: The same failure reproduces with the grid executor and no Nav2 action at all (baseline-dds-*), and does NOT reproduce over UDP at the same N (baseline-udp-*). Nav2 serialised execution is therefore not the cause.
mechanism.tickRateIsTheHiddenVariable: Because the failure is transport-throughput-bound, whether a given N passes depends on how slowly its ticks happen to run. N=6 Nav2 passed only because Nav2 actions throttled the tick rate below the transport ceiling; at N=7/N=8 no ownership was ever formed, so no Nav2 action ran, ticks ran fast, message rate rose, and the fleet locked into a backlog it could never drain.
mechanism.volumeDriver: Every peer re-announced EVERY known task on EVERY tick. The receiver ignores an announce for a task it already has, so this is pure waste, and it makes per-tick traffic O(N^2 x tasks): at N=8 with 8 tasks that is ~504 Fast DDS publications per tick.
mechanism.measuredTransportCeiling: N=8 DDS + grid: settle 8ms -> remote lag 105-140 ticks (unbounded backlog); settle 25ms -> lag 8-9 ticks; settle 116ms -> lag 4 ticks and all peers live. Lag is a direct function of message rate.
